title: Programmable Emission Protocol: Acceptance Criteria for Typed Frames, Stream Integrity, and Tool Fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD-level acceptance criteria for a new emission protocol that formalizes typed frames (envelopes), stream integrity guarantees, resume/checkpoint semantics, and deterministic tool-call fallback behavior. This ticket aligns product requirements with engineering test cases and rollout gating for Hosted API + Dedicated runtime. Focus: clear, testable criteria for schema validation, partial emission handling, error classification, idempotent tool handoff, and end-to-end observability keys.
background: Many existing spec artifacts cover pieces of structured output and tool calls but lack a concise checklist that combines: (1) how typed frames propagate across streaming boundaries, (2) how resumable checkpoints are represented, (3) deterministic fallback ordering for tool invocations when model output deviates, and (4) telemetry hooks required for post-deploy regression detection. This ticket consolidates product decisions and acceptance tests so engineering can implement and QA the work without iterative scope clarifications.
requirements: All emitted frames must be wrapped in a typed envelope with stable 'frame_type' and 'frame_id' fields.
Streaming responses expose explicit boundary markers: FRAME_START, FRAME_PART, FRAME_END; clients can reconstruct frames deterministically.
Partial/aborted frames must include a checkpoint token that allows resume semantics for clients in the same session ID.
Tool/function call intents emitted mid-stream must contain a call-hash, expected idempotency key, and a minimal call-spec payload (name + args schema reference).

Fallbacks: when primary tool invocation is rejected (validation or capacity), the runtime must attempt a configured fallback list in priority order and include a fallback_trace array in final metadata.
Per-request telemetry metadata keys (request_id, model_variant, route, frame_count, call_count) must be attached to emitted telemetry events and logs.

Error classes are enumerated as recoverable, transient, and terminal; recoverable errors permit automatic retry of the frame or tool call, transient errors require backoff, and terminal errors cause stream termination with a structured error object.
All schema references must be semantic versioned; runtime will accept older minor versions only if compatibility rules apply and include an 'accepted_schema_version' in response metadata.
Clients receiving a terminal error must be provided a human-readable 'error_hint' and machine-readable 'error_code' for automated handling.
Rollout must include a canary policy: 1% of traffic for 48h, validate telemetry, then 10% for 24h before full rollout.
Observability: a new dashboard must surface frame-level failure rates, tool fallback counts, resume success rate, and average time-to-first-frame.
Backwards compatibility: existing non-framed streaming users continue to receive tokens as before unless they opt in to framed mode via a header parameter.
API surface: SDKs expose a 'streamFrames' helper that translates framed events into an ordered stream of typed objects with resume helpers.
Privacy: checkpoint tokens do not leak PII; tokens are opaque handles referencing server-side state and must be encrypted at rest.
Performance SLOs: adding framed envelopes must not increase median token latency by more than 5% on standard Hosted routes.
Failure telemetry must include traceable links to GitHub PRs and config versions when available for faster incident triage.
Acceptance tests must be runnable in CI and cover both Hosted and Dedicated runtime variants.
Documentation: developer guide, schema registry entry, and SDK examples must be published before wide rollout.
non_goals: This ticket does not redesign the function-calling argument schema language; it assumes current JSON schema approach.
It does not implement on-prem data plane encryption changes beyond storing checkpoint tokens encrypted at rest.
It does not add new billing dimensions for framed vs unframed streams in this milestone.
acceptance_criteria: Typed envelope validation: Given a sample of 500 streamed sessions, >= 99% of frames must include valid 'frame_type' and 'frame_id' fields and pass schema checks in CI.
Stream integrity: Clients can reassemble streamed frames with no out-of-order gaps when network reordering is simulated; end-to-end checksum matches within test harness.
Resume semantics: Simulated network disconnect and resume with checkpoint token results in correct continuation 95% of the time across Hosted and Dedicated testbeds.
Tool call idempotency: Replaying a tool call with the same call-hash must not produce duplicate external side effects within a 24-hour window in the integration test environment.

Fallback ordering: When primary tool is intentionally made unavailable, the system executes fallbacks in configured order and returns fallback_trace with at least one successful entry in 90% of tests.
Error classification: Injected error types map to recoverable, transient, or terminal buckets as defined and produce the expected retry/backoff behavior in automated tests.
Observability signals: Dashboard shows frame_error_rate, fallback_rate, resume_success_rate with synthetic traffic; alerts fire when metrics exceed thresholds defined in PRD.
SDK behavior: 'streamFrames' helper reconstructs frames, exposes resume() and cancel() methods, and matches behavior documented in SDK examples.
Latency impact: End-to-end median TTF (time-to-first-token) increase <= 5% on the standard perf harness within noise bounds.
Security: Checkpoint tokens are encrypted at rest and decrypted only by the serving process; no plain tokens appear in logs in canary runs.
Docs and examples are published and linked from the API reference with at least one worked integration example (server-side handler invoking a fallback tool).
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope serializer/deserializer covering missing fields, extra fields, and version negotiation.
Integration test that simulates long-running streamed responses and client resume from checkpoints under packet loss.
Chaos tests: inject transient failures into tool gateway and verify fallback_trace contents and retry/backoff behavior.
End-to-end contract test: SDK + Hosted route + sample tool that mutates a read-only test store to validate idempotency semantics.
Performance regression test running framed vs unframed payloads under p95 concurrency targets.
notes: Decision: prefer simple opaque checkpoint tokens rather than resending large prefix state to clients.
PM will coordinate a joint review with SDK owners and security for the token encryption approach.
Include a migration plan for partners using the Dedicated runtime to opt into framed mode without downtime.
